title: Who are you
description: Introduce yourself, and say who other people are.
grammar: subject pronouns and the verb ser
grammarNote: The pronoun comes before the verb: yo soy, tú eres, él es.

explanation.summary: Spanish has five subject pronouns where English has three, and the verb ser is irregular in every form that matters. The two things a learner gets wrong first are dropping the pronoun and using the wrong one for usted.

sections.heading: Five pronouns
sections.body: Yo, tú, él, ella, usted. He and she are two different words in Spanish, and usted is a polite form that is also the third person singular. A beginner can drop the pronoun when the verb makes it obvious, but it is safer to use it: yo soy estudiante is much clearer than soy estudiante.

sections.heading: Ser is irregular
sections.body: Only the yo form is regular: soy. The rest change: eres, es, somos, sois, son. The same verbs change in every tense, and you will meet those forms later in the path. There is also another form, eres for tú and usted is the polite third person with es.

sections.heading: Saying what someone does
sections.body: There is a third verb for what you are doing, and it is not ser. Working and studying are what you do, and they use estar: estoy trabajando, estoy estudiando. But a profession uses ser: soy profesor. The difference is that a profession is what you are, and a place is where you are: soy de Madrid, estoy en Madrid.

items.note: Its forms are irregular: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son.
Masculine: el estudiante. The feminine is la estudiante.
Masculine: el profesor. The feminine is la profesora.
Masculine: el amigo. The feminine is la amiga.

drills.note: The pronoun comes before the verb.
Él is masculine, ella is feminine.
